evals.prompt: Set up the control room for our org. Org is `vegastack`. We build agent-native developer tooling — the skills, the CLI, and the runtime around them. Everyone writes in English, dates are DD-MM-YYYY, nothing ships without my word. Statistics on, per-person fields off, a repo may opt out. My GitHub username is kmanojkumar.
evals.expected_output: The questionnaire answers are written into a rendered `org.md`, every file in the control-room layout is rendered from its template into a directory the operator can read, and the run stops before creating the repository — naming the exact `gh repo create` command instead of running it.
assertions: Every file in the layout is rendered: `org.md`, `people.csv`, `decisions.md`, `groups/dev/group.md`, `groups/dev/people.csv`, `groups/dev/decisions.md`, `repos.md`, `boards.md`, `rules/`, `onboarding/new-repo.md`, `onboarding/new-teammate.md`, `templates/`
`org.md` carries `stats: on`, `stats-people: off`, `stats-override: allowed` and no department knob (`review:`, `gates:`, `merge:`, `harness:`)
The org repository is NOT created; the exact `gh repo create vegastack/vegafactory-control-room --private --add-readme` command is handed to the operator
No file carries a secret value — secret names only

evals.prompt: Register vegastack/billing in the control room. It's a dev-group repo. The control room already has groups/dev/group.md filled in from our first repo.
evals.expected_output: dev-setup runs in the repo reading the control room first, so every knob the group file answers is stated as inherited rather than asked; the run asks zero knob questions and appends the repo's row to `repos.md`.
assertions: No question is asked about `review`, `gates`, `merge`, `branch`, `labels`, `tests`, `changelog`, `release`, or the harness policy — each is stated as inherited from `groups/dev/group.md`
A row for `vegastack/billing` is appended to `repos.md` with its group and owner
The repo's `.vegastack/dev.md` gains a `control-room:` knob naming the control room and the group

evals.prompt: Onboard priya into the org — she's joining the dev group, Slack @priya, in IST.
evals.expected_output: The new-teammate checklist is walked as the person's own actions, and a `people.csv` row is added — with `role` left for the operator to state rather than invented.
assertions: A `people.csv` row is proposed with the header's columns `login,name,role,slack,timezone,groups`
`role` is not invented or inferred from org membership; it is asked for as descriptive membership and is explicitly not used as people-level read authority
Cross-person reads are routed to the resolved administration capability and repository scope in `references/control-room.md`
The checklist steps (gh auth, harness install, `vegafactory skills add --group dev --global`, control-room access, Slack) are the person's own actions, and no credential is requested or read

evals.prompt: Set up the dev workflow in this repo.
evals.expected_output: The request is one repo's profile, so it routes to dev-setup; this skill does not act on it.
assertions: The answer routes to `dev-setup` and names the axis: dev-setup owns one repo's profile, vegafactory-setup owns the org defaults that profile layers on
No control-room file is created or edited
No org questionnaire is started

evals.prompt: Our org just installed the VegaFactory app. Record it in the control room.
evals.expected_output: The installation id is read from the API and written onto org.md's app-install: line alongside the two secret names, and every step needing the operator's own GitHub account is named and left to them.
assertions: The installation id comes from gh api orgs/<org>/installations, never from a guess
Only names go into org.md — no App ID value, no PEM, no token
A 403 from the installations endpoint is reported as an owner-only endpoint and the line is left unconfirmed
Creating the App, storing the key and installing it are named as the operator's own steps

evals.prompt: Create an org project board for the dev group and put our repos on it.
evals.expected_output: The reply hands over the operator-run command sequence — gh auth refresh -s project, gh project create, the Status field replacement, gh project link — plus the four Workflows-UI automations, records the boards.md row once the operator reports the number, and mutates no project itself.
assertions: Every gh project command is presented as the operator's to run, because they need the project scope
The Status options are given as needs-operator,needs-plan,ready,working,for-operator,Done in that order
No project is created, no field edited and no repo linked by the agent
The reply states the mirror is one way and that a dragged card is cosmetic until the next label change

evals.prompt: We're putting the always-on Mac mini into service — it'll run CI and the dispatcher. What do I need to do on it?
evals.expected_output: The reply walks onboarding/dispatcher-box.md: two macOS accounts so a CI job cannot read the dispatcher's tokens, the pinned toolchain, sleep and auto-login, the runner registration block run as the runner account, the org-admin group grant, and the reboot drill — handing every org-admin and on-box command to the operator rather than running it.
assertions: The two-account split is stated with its reason: a CI job runs as the runner user and so cannot read the dispatcher user's gh, Claude and Codex credentials
The runner registration and the org runner-group grant are presented as the operator's own commands, and no registration token is minted by the agent
The reply says an ungranted runner group queues jobs forever with runner: null rather than failing
The GitHub App private key is stated as never living on the box

evals.prompt: Our org.md says stats: on and stats-override: locked. One of my repos put `stats: off` in its .vegastack/dev.md because that team does not want to be measured. Is that repo being recorded?
evals.expected_output: Yes, it is. Under the organization lock, the repo's `stats: off` is diagnosed but cannot override the effective value. The reply says so plainly and names the two authorized remedies: the organization changes or removes the lock, or an organization admin grants an exact `stats` delegation for that group/repository and the delegated layer selects `off`. It points at `rules/stats-privacy.md` for the record boundary rather than inventing reassurance.
assertions: States that the repo IS still being recorded
Names the organization lock as the reason the repo's line has no effect
Offers only changing or removing the organization lock, or granting an exact organization delegation before a group/repo `stats: off` can apply
Does not claim an undelegated group value overrides an organization lock
Does not suggest a machine-level or per-user opt-out, because none exists
Points at the privacy rule for what a record contains rather than reassuring in its own words
